question.text: The principle of 'tax neutrality' in AIF structuring means:

answer.text: The AIF itself pays no tax on any of its income.
All AIF income is taxed at the maximum marginal rate at the fund level.
SEBI guarantees a tax refund for all AIF investors every year.
The investor should not be in a WORSE tax position by investing through the AIF than by investing directly at the investor level.

explanation.text: The Logic: Tax neutrality means investors should not face a comparatively adverse tax position by pooling their capital through an AIF compared with investing directly. Per the workbook (page 98), tax neutrality is the principle that avoids placing investors in a worse position than direct investment, and page 103 confirms investors should not be subject to higher taxes than if they invested directly. For Cat I/II AIFs, Section 115UB pass-through applies to income OTHER than business income; business income is taxed at the fund level and is exempt in the investors' hands. The Trap: 'No tax at fund' overstates the position - Cat III AIFs are taxed at the fund level, and Cat I/II business income is taxed at fund level too. The MMR-at-fund description applies to Cat III taxation, not 'neutrality'. The SEBI refund claim is fabricated. Note: Per page 302 of the workbook, Cat I/II pass-through under Section 115UB applies to income other than business income. Business income earned by Cat I/II AIFs is taxable at the fund level and is then exempt in the investors' hands when distributed.
